{"body":"`docs/research/ios-27.md` §2.1. Both halves are left over from #56, and they share one property:
**the snapshot suite cannot see either of them.** Neither is a reference that moved; both need the
app in front of you.

They are together in one issue for that reason, and because both land in the same overlay chrome.
Split them if the resizability half grows.

Two things changed with #56 and make this worth doing now. Resizability turns itself on when the
app is built against the iOS 27 SDK, so a resized window is reachable today. And the references are
recorded against iOS 27 on `main`, so a change here produces an attributable diff — which is exactly
what was impossible while ~1600 of them were moving at once.

## 1. Resizability and `dockBleed`

`Sources/ReachyUI/FloatingViewportModifier.swift:130-180`. `dockBleed` picks its edge from
`UIWindowScene.interfaceOrientation`, and under iOS 27 orientation is a preference rather than a
contract — iPhone Mirroring reports portrait whatever the window's shape.

The analysis says this degrades to nothing rather than to something wrong. The branch chooses only
*which* side; the amount always comes from `geometry.safeAreaInsets`:

- a mis-reported orientation falls to `default: .none`, the neutral value;
- a window away from a screen edge has no safe-area inset, so either side bleeds by zero.

The wrong-side case needs a window at a screen edge **and** an orientation reported for the opposite
one. That is reasoning, not a measurement, and nothing in the repository reaches a resized window:
no preview forces landscape, and `FloatingViewportGeometryTests` takes `bleed` as a value already
decided — as the source comment at `FloatingViewportModifier.swift:130-148` says outright.

**To settle it:** an XCUITest that sets `XCUIDevice.shared.orientation`, or the app in iPhone
Mirroring and in an iPad split view. Confirm the dock meets the screen edge in each. If the analysis
holds, the outcome is a test and a comment, not a fix.

While you are there, the rest of the resizability checklist has no coverage either: no reference
exercises a narrow or a wide window, because `Apps/.prefire.yml` pins two fixed `ViewImageConfig`
sizes (`iPhone 16 Pro`, `iPad Pro 11`).

## 2. The `.soft` scroll edge

`Sources/ReachyDesign/ReachyChrome.swift:47`, one consumer at `Sources/ReachyUI/LogConsoleView.swift:74`.

`ScrollEdgeEffectStyle.automatic` was revised in 27 and Apple asks for explicit overrides to be
reviewed. The modifier itself survives in the SDK (`.automatic` / `.hard` / `.soft`), so the
availability gate needs nothing.

Whether `.soft` still beats the new `.automatic` cannot be answered from a reference. The effect
draws where content passes under a bar, and the preview renders no bar —
`Console-installer-log-iPhone-16-Pro` is a plain page of log text. Recording a variant would compare
two identical images, the same way glass is invisible headless.

**To settle it:** `mise run device`, open the log console, scroll it under the navigation bar, and
compare `.soft` against `.automatic`. Keep whichever reads better and record the reason beside the

# iOS 27, Xcode 27 and this app

Issues #56, #57, #58 and #74 all cite `docs/research/apple-ecosystem-growth.md`. That file is in no commit and in
no branch — the reasoning behind the P0 label lives only in the issue bodies. This file replaces it. It records
what the SDK move demands, what was measured on a local Xcode 27 install, and which of the audit's findings
survived a check against the code.

Everything below was verified against the tree at the time of writing. Claims that did **not** survive are kept and
marked, because a corrected claim is worth more than a deleted one.

## §0 The SDK move

### Measured on Xcode 27.0 Beta 6 (27A5252f), 2026-08-29

| Task                         | Result                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mise run build:app` (macOS) | 0 errors. `actool` compiles the macOS variant of the Icon Composer `.icon`                      |
| `mise run build:app:ios`     | 0 errors, widget controls included                                                              |
| `mise run snapshots:build`   | `** TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED **`, 0 errors, artifact `…_iphonesimulator27.0-arm64-x86_64.xctestrun` |

**No source change was necessary.** See `@ContentBuilder` below for why one was expected and did not arrive.

New warnings, all from Swift 6.3 rather than from the SDK: 42 × `NonSendableSuperclass` in the Prefire-generated
test classes (the forked `PreviewTests.stencil` writes them), and 5 × `SendingRisksDataRace` in `ReachyMedia`
(`RobotCallController.swift:251,267,286`, `ConversationDelegateAdapter.swift:46,52`). They are warnings today and
an error in a later language mode.

### `@ContentBuilder` is not an adoption task

`ContentBuilder` is a type alias for `ViewBuilder`. The win comes from the SDK rebuilding its own shared components
around `TupleContent`, which carries no domain until its elements give it one, so `Group { Group { … } }` no longer
multiplies the overload search at every level. Published measurements put a five-level
`Section → Group → ForEach` at 1 050 052 constraint scopes / 11.06 s under Xcode 26.6 against 189 / 26.97 ms under
Xcode 27 beta 4.

Three consequences for this repository:

- The improvement arrives with the SDK. There is nothing to annotate, so the separate commit issue #56 budgets for
  `Sources/ReachyUI/Previews/**` and `Apps/ReachyStorybook` has no content.
- The real cost runs the other way. Once the builder stops supplying a protocol for every expression, calls that

== §2.1 ==
## §2 Gaps the P0 issues do not cover

Each row was checked against the tree.

| Gap                                             | Where                                                                                                                           | Note                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Resizability audit                              | `Sources/ReachyUI/FloatingViewportModifier.swift:142-180`                                                                       | **Analysed, no change made.** See §2.1                                                 |

| Menu icons ~~needs `preferredImageVisibility`~~ | `Menu {` in `LogConsoleView`, `SceneViewport`, `SoundboardScreen`, `AppStoreScreen`, `LiveTab`, `RobotFilesScreen`              | **Closed — nothing to do.** See §2.1                                                   |

| Snapshot coverage is two fixed sizes            | `Apps/.prefire.yml` (`iPhone 16 Pro`, `iPad Pro 11`)                                                                            | under resizability no reference exercises a narrow or a wide window                    |
| The combined privacy prompt                     | camera, microphone, Bluetooth, local network and location in one dialog                                                         | the first-run gate and the smoke test that walks it may both shift                     |
| Stricter TLS                                    | `ws://<host>:8443`, `Sources/ReachyKit/Transport/CameraSignalingClient.swift:4`, plus `NSAllowsLocalNetworking`                 | signaling is plaintext                                                                 |
| macOS 27 drops Intel                            | `Scripts/release-macos.sh`                                                                                                      | the universal slice stops being obligatory                                             |

### §2.1 The three visual rows, resolved

**Menu icons — closed, nothing to do.** `preferredImageVisibility` is UIKit only. It is a property of
`UIMenuElement` and `UIMenuLeaf` (`UIMenuElement.h:68`, `UIMenuLeaf.h:33`, `API_AVAILABLE(ios(27.0))`), and SwiftUI
exposes no counterpart — its `swiftinterface` has no `ImageVisibility` of any spelling, and its only menu modifiers
are `menuOrder`, `menuActionDismissBehavior` and `menuIndicator`. Every menu here is a SwiftUI `Menu`, so there is
no knob to set. Re-open this row only when SwiftUI ships one.

**The `.soft` scroll edge — open, and not a code task.** The modifier survives in the 27 SDK
(`ScrollEdgeEffectStyle.automatic` / `.hard` / `.soft`), so the availability gate needs nothing. Whether `.soft` is
still the better choice than the revised `.automatic` cannot be settled here: the effect draws where content passes
under a bar, and the preview renders no bar. `Console-installer-log-iPhone-16-Pro` is a plain page of log text.
Re-recording a variant would compare two identical images. This needs the app on a device, with the log console
open, exactly as glass does.

**Resizability and `dockBleed` — analysed, and left alone.** The concern is real in shape: `dockBleed` picks its
edge from `UIWindowScene.interfaceOrientation`, and under 27 orientation is a preference. But the failure degrades
to nothing rather than to something wrong, because the branch only chooses _which_ side, while the amount always
comes from `geometry.safeAreaInsets`:

- a mis-reported orientation falls to `default: .none`, which is the neutral value;
- a window away from the screen edge has no safe-area inset, so either side bleeds by zero.

The wrong-side case would need a window at a screen edge _and_ an orientation reported for the opposite one. Not
measured, because nothing here reaches a resized window: no preview forces landscape, and
`FloatingViewportGeometryTests` takes `bleed` as a value already decided — which the source comment at
`FloatingViewportModifier.swift:130-148` states outright. What would settle it is an XCUITest that sets
`XCUIDevice.shared.orientation`, or the app in iPhone Mirroring. Until then this is reasoning, not a measurement.

Searched for and **absent**, so not problems: `UIScreen.main`, `userInterfaceIdiom`, the deprecated `UIApplication`
status-bar accessors, `MXMetricManager`, On Demand Resources, `.onMove`.

## §3 New API worth having

Ordered by how close each sits to something the app already does.

- **Toolbars.** `visibilityPriority(_:)`, `ToolbarOverflowMenu`, `ToolbarItem(placement: .topBarPinnedTrailing)`,
  `toolbarMinimizeBehavior(_:for:)`, `ToolbarPlacement.statusBar`, `ForEach` and `EmptyView` inside toolbar
  builders. The direct remedy for a toolbar in a narrow window, which resizability now makes reachable.
- **`.reorderable()` + `.reorderContainer(for:)`** — reordering in any container. The known-robots list has no
  `.onMove` today.
- **`swipeActionsContainer()`** — swipe actions outside `List`, so a `LazyVGrid` can carry them.
- **`systemExtraLargePortrait`** — a new widget family on iOS, iPadOS and macOS 27.
- **Live Activities**: `supplementalActivityFamilies([.small])` puts an activity on Apple Watch and the CarPlay
  dashboard **without a watchOS app**, which covers much of #75 from inside #61; a landscape Dynamic Island
  (`isDynamicIslandLimitedInWidth`); StandBy.
- **App Intents**: `LongRunningIntent`, `CancellableIntent`, `ExecutionTargets`, `EntityCollection`,
  `SyncableEntity`, `RelevantEntities`, `@UnionValue`, and **`AppIntentsTesting`**, which drives intents through the
  real system paths. Nine controls plus Siri, Spotlight and Handoff are covered only indirectly today.
- **Foundation Models**: the `LanguageModel` / `LanguageModelExecutor` protocols make one session work against the
  on-device model, Private Cloud Compute, MLX and third-party providers, which turns the on-device-or-cloud question
  in #72 and #73 from an architectural choice into configuration. Evaluations and the token-count API are new.
- **ARKit object tracking reaches iOS** with the visionOS API, so #77 is a shipped feature rather than a bet.
- `AsyncImage(request:)` with HTTP caching, for `HFAvatar` — the one network image in the app.
- `@Environment(\.appearsActive)` for the inactive Mac window; a sidebar on iPhone for the five-tab shell
  (`.sidebarAdaptable` is already set, `Sources/ReachyUI/Shell/ReachyTabShell.swift:120`); the Now Playing framework
  for the soundboard.

## §4 Order

`#57` → the resizability audit → `#56` → chrome and `.soft` → `preferredImageVisibility`. Everything in §3 waits
until the tree is green again.

  13     /// `tabBarMinimizeBehavior` itself for macOS 26 — so reading the method's

  16     /// `@available(macOS, unavailable)`. The method compiles there and has nothing

  21     /// minimised bar shrank into the row that strip already occupied and the whole
  22     /// tab bar read as having been replaced by it. The dock is a tab accessory now,
  23     /// which is the slot the shrinking makes room for, so minimising is the
  24     /// interaction rather than the thing that breaks it. Do not reintroduce the
  25     /// argument; see `ReachyTabAccessory`.
  26     @ViewBuilder
  27     func reachyMinimizingTabBar() -> some View {
  28         #if os(iOS)
  29             if #available(iOS 26.0, *) {
  30                 tabBarMinimizeBehavior(.onScrollDown)
  31             } else {
  32                 self
  33             }
  34         #else
  35             self
  36         #endif
  37     }
  38

  42     /// under a navigation bar. A grouped `Form` already ends in its own background,
  43     /// and softening that edge blurs a boundary the reader uses.
  44     @ViewBuilder
  45     func reachySoftScrollEdge(_ edges: Edge.Set) -> some View {
  46         if #available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, *) {
  47             scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.soft, for: edges)
  48         } else {
  49             self
  50         }
  51     }
  52 }

content.text:
Разобрался в issue и в коде. Ключевая находка, которой в issue нет: в SDK 27 `UIWindowScene.interfaceOrientation` **помечен deprecated** (`ios(13.0, 26.0)`) в пользу `effectiveGeometry.interfaceOrientation` — а именно эту строку и читает `dockBleed` ([FloatingViewportModifier.swift:180](Sources/ReachyUI/FloatingViewportModifier.swift:180)).

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `effectiveGeometry` доступен с iOS 16, deployment target тут 18.0 — значит замена не требует `#available` вообще, это буквально одна строка.
- В репозитории **нет iOS-хостед unit-test раннера**: `mise run test` — это SwiftPM на macOS, а весь `dockBleed` живёт под `#if !os(macOS)`. Единственные iOS-бандлы — `ReachyMiniUITests` (XCUITest) и `ReachyUISnapshotTests`. Поэтому «тест», о котором просит issue, стоит дороже, чем кажется.
- Рецепт standalone-пробника уже записан в [AGENTS.md:104-120](Sources/ReachyUI/AGENTS.md:104) — включая ловушку с `UIRequiresFullScreen` на iPad. Ровно её снятие и даёт resized window, который issue просит измерить.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

questions.question: Часть 1 (dockBleed): если замер подтвердит анализ — насколько далеко идём в коде?

options.label: Замер + свап на effectiveGeometry
options.description: Прогоняю пробник в resized window, записываю числа в комментарий/AGENTS.md/ios-27.md и меняю одну строку: scene.interfaceOrientation → scene.effectiveGeometry.interfaceOrientation (снимает deprecation, это ответ Apple именно для resized window). Без нового теста.

options.label: Только замер и комментарий
options.description: Строго то, что просит issue минус тест: пробник, числа, обновлённые комментарии и docs. Код не трогаем — deprecated-вызов остаётся до отдельной задачи.

options.label: Замер + свап + тест на маппинг
options.description: Дополнительно выношу чистую функцию bleed(for:insets:) и закрепляю четыре случая тестом. Но жить он может только в iOS-бандле ReachyUISnapshotTests — там сейчас нет ни одного рукописного теста, смешение назначений.

# Issue #114 — settle the resized window and the `.soft` scroll edge

## Context

Two leftovers from the iOS 27 SDK move (#56) that **the snapshot suite cannot see**: neither is a
reference that moved, both need a running app. They are settled together because both land in the
same overlay chrome, and because `main` now records its references against iOS 27 — so a change here
produces an attributable diff.

1. `dockBleed` reads the window scene's interface orientation to pick *which* screen edge the docked
   tab reaches for. Under iOS 27 orientation is a preference, not a contract. The analysis in
   `docs/research/ios-27.md` §2.1 says this degrades to nothing rather than to something wrong — but
   that is reasoning, never a measurement, because nothing in the repository reaches a resized window.
2. `.soft` scroll edge over the log console. Whether it still beats the revised `.automatic` cannot
   be answered from a reference: the effect draws where content passes under a bar, and the preview
   renders no bar.

## Established before planning

- **`UIWindowScene.interfaceOrientation` is deprecated in the 27 SDK** —
  `API_DEPRECATED("Use effectiveGeometry.interfaceOrientation instead.", ios(13.0, 26.0))`
  (`UIWindowScene.h:26`). `effectiveGeometry` is `API_AVAILABLE(ios(16.0))` and the deployment target
  here is iOS 18.0, so the replacement needs **no availability gate**. This is the one line
  [FloatingViewportModifier.swift:180](Sources/ReachyUI/FloatingViewportModifier.swift:180) calls.
  No warning fires today only because the deprecation window closes at 26.0 and the target is 18.0.
- **There is no iOS-hosted unit-test runner.** `mise run test` is SwiftPM on macOS, and all of
  `dockBleed` lives under `#if !os(macOS)`. The only iOS bundles are `ReachyMiniUITests` (XCUITest)
  and `ReachyUISnapshotTests`. So the "test" the issue imagines costs more than it looks; the
  house precedent for this exact question is measurement recorded in `AGENTS.md`
  ([AGENTS.md:104-120](Sources/ReachyUI/AGENTS.md:104) already carries the probe recipe, including
  the `UIRequiresFullScreen` trap that *is* the resized window).
- **The attached iPhone runs iOS 26.5.2**, the simulators run 27.0. So iPhone Mirroring cannot
  produce an iOS 27 resized window — that measurement is simulator-only. The device pass is for
  `.soft` legibility on real glass, and it sees iOS 26's `.automatic`, not 27's.
- 408 previews × 2 devices × 2 appearances = **1632 references, 201 MB in LFS**. A third
  `snapshot_devices` entry adds **+816 PNGs, roughly +100 MB** — larger than the "~500" figure quoted
  when the question was asked. Flagged, and carried out as decided.

## 1. Measure the resized window

Rebuild the standalone probe per the recipe in [AGENTS.md:104](Sources/ReachyUI/AGENTS.md:104) —
outside the repository, bare `swiftc`, `UILaunchScreen` in its `Info.plist`. Extend its HUD to print,
side by side:

- `scene.interfaceOrientation` (the deprecated reading the code uses today)
- `scene.effectiveGeometry.interfaceOrientation` (the replacement)
- `geometry.size`, `geometry.safeAreaInsets`, and the `EdgeBleed` the current `switch` yields

Configurations, in this order — the first two certify the probe before any new number is believed:

| Run | Device | Expected control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | iPhone 17 Pro, portrait | reader 402 × 778, t62 b34 (already recorded in the source comment) |
| 2 | iPhone 17 Pro, both landscape cases via `UISupportedInterfaceOrientations` | 750 × 382, l62 r62 |
| 3 | iPad Pro 11, **`UIRequiresFullScreen` omitted** — the resized window | the measurement |
| 4 | iPad Pro 11, `UIRequiresFullScreen` set | full-screen control |

Run 3 is the whole point: resize the window narrow and wide, and portrait- and landscape-shaped, and
read whether the two orientation readings **disagree**, and whether `safeAreaInsets.leading/trailing`
is ever non-zero there. Non-zero insets plus a wrong orientation is the only failing case; zero
insets confirm the analysis.

## 2. Apply the outcome to `dockBleed`

`Sources/ReachyUI/FloatingViewportModifier.swift`

- Swap the one line to `scene.effectiveGeometry.interfaceOrientation` — un-deprecates the call and is
  Apple's own answer for a resized window. No `#available`, no behaviour change expected on iPhone.
- Replace the "not measured" half of the doc comment at lines 131-148 with the numbers from step 1,
  keeping the existing `.landscapeLeft` / `.landscapeRight` explanation, which is still the load-
  bearing part.
- Update [AGENTS.md](Sources/ReachyUI/AGENTS.md) (the `dockBleed` bullet) and
  [docs/research/ios-27.md](docs/research/ios-27.md) §2 / §2.1: the resizability row moves from
  "analysed, no change made" to measured, and the §4 order line loses that step.

If step 1 *does* find a disagreement with non-zero insets, stop and report before writing a fix —
the corrective branch cannot come from geometry (both landscape sides report the same inset), so it
would be a design question, not a patch.

## 3. `.soft` versus `.automatic`

Simulator A/B first, because iOS 27's revised `.automatic` only exists there:

1. `mise run storybook` on `iPhone 17 Pro` / 27.0, open **"Console — installer log"** — dense
   monospaced lines under a real navigation bar, which is exactly the case the modifier is for
   ([LogConsoleViewPreviews.swift:8](Sources/ReachyUI/Previews/LogConsoleViewPreviews.swift:8)).
2. Scroll it with the iOS Simulator control tool (`swipe`), so the text passes under the bar, and
   screenshot. `simctl` alone cannot inject touches; if the control tool is unavailable, the fallback
   is a throwaway XCUITest that swipes and attaches a screenshot.
3. Flip `reachySoftScrollEdge` to `.automatic` in
   [ReachyChrome.swift:47](Sources/ReachyDesign/ReachyChrome.swift:47), rebuild, repeat at the same
   offset, and **quantify** the difference over the band under the bar rather than eyeballing it
   (delta + bounding box, the way reference diffs are measured here).
4. Report both crops with the numbers and a recommendation, then build to the phone
   (`mise run device`) with the recommended variant so the final call is made on real glass.
5. Whichever wins, record the reason beside the modifier — its doc comment already says why the
   override exists, so this is one added sentence, not a new paragraph.

## 4. Narrow-window snapshot coverage

`Apps/.prefire.yml` — add a third entry to `snapshot_devices`. The narrowest size the stencil's
mapping reaches is `iPhone SE (1st generation)` → `.iPhoneSe`, 320 pt wide
([PreviewTests.stencil:248](Apps/ReachyUISnapshotTests/PreviewTests.stencil:248)); that is the right
proxy for a narrow resized window.

Note what this does and does not buy: the stencil sets `snapshot.device.safeArea = .zero`, so a
narrow reference proves **layout at narrow width** and can never see `dockBleed`. It is coverage for
the rest of the resizability checklist, not for step 1.

Sequence, which matters because `record` deletes every PNG before it runs anything:

```bash
./bin/mise run snapshots:build
```

then `test:snapshots` to see the current state, then `test:snapshots:record`, then verify the count
recovered before trusting anything:

```bash
find Apps/ReachyUISnapshotTests -path '*__Snapshots__*' -name '*.png' | wc -l
```

Expect 2448 (1632 + 816). A successful record reports every test as failed — that is what a clean
recording looks like; `git status -- '*__Snapshots__*'` is what says what moved. The new PNGs need an
explicit `git add`; no hook stages them.

## Verification

- `./bin/mise run build:app:ios` and `build:app` — the `effectiveGeometry` swap is under
  `#if !os(macOS)`, so both platforms must compile.
- `./bin/mise run lint` and `format-check`.
- `./bin/mise run test` — the SwiftPM suites, unaffected but cheap.
- `./bin/mise run test:snapshots` after recording — must pass with nothing written.
- The probe HUD numbers for runs 1 and 2 must reproduce the figures already recorded in
  `FloatingViewportModifier.swift` and `AGENTS.md`. If they do not, the probe is wrong and its
  landscape and resized-window numbers are worthless.
- The phone build installed and the log console opened, for the `.soft` call.

## Out of scope

- Any `dockBleed` behaviour change beyond the deprecation swap — gated on what step 1 measures.
- A `bleed(for:insets:)` extraction plus unit test: it has no runner on iOS and would have to be
  smuggled into the snapshot bundle. The probe, not a test, is what caught the inverted mapping.
- iPhone Mirroring — the attached phone is on iOS 26.5.2 and cannot produce the iOS 27 case.

input.tldr: Three preview references on main capture an emptied screen instead of the state they are named for, because only the first device size rendered keeps the seeded model state.
input.prompt:
In reachy-mini-swift, three snapshot references verify the wrong state, and the cause is pre-existing on `main` (found while working issue #114, not caused by it).

`Apps/ReachyUISnapshotTests/PreviewTests.stencil` renders the SAME preview instance once per entry in `snapshot_devices` (`Apps/.prefire.yml`), in a loop that reassigns `snapshot.device` between renders. For three previews, only the FIRST render shows the seeded state; every later render captures an emptied screen:

- `Device check — robots found` (`Apps/ReachyMini/Previews/DeviceCheckViewPreviews.swift:23`) — seeded with `RobotBrowser.preview()`, which sets `servicesByType` to two services. The `iPhone 16 Pro` reference (first device) shows `reachy-mini-4f2a` / `reachy-mini-9c81`; the `iPad Pro 11` reference shows **"No robots found"**. - `Device check — permission denied` — same file, same shape.
- `Controller — recording` (`MoveRecorderPreviewsTests`) — the bottom third of the frame differs.

Reproduce: put a third entry FIRST in `snapshot_devices` (e.g. `iPhone SE (1st generation)`), run `mise run test:snapshots:record`, and exactly those three `iPhone-16-Pro` references change — the state moves to whichever device is listed first. Put the new entry last and nothing moves.

`RobotBrowser.init()` is empty and `start()` is explicit, and `DeviceCheckView` guards its `onAppear` on `browsesLiveNetwork: false`, so the seeded value is not being overwritten by a live browse — find what actually resets it across renders (a fresh `@State`/`@Observable` instance per render is the first suspect, since the stencil re-renders one `PrefireSnapshot`).

Outcome wanted: every device size captures the state its preview is named for. Then re-record and check that those three iPad/SE references gain the content they are missing.

Issue #114 разобран. Обе половины сняты с работающего приложения.

## 1. `dockBleed` в изменяемом окне

Пробник по рецепту из `AGENTS.md`, расширенный печатью обоих чтений ориентации рядом с insets:

| Конфигурация | reader | insets | ориентация | bleed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone 17 Pro, полный экран, portrait | 402 × 778 | t62 b34 **l0 r0** | portrait | none |
| iPhone 17 Pro, landscapeLeft | 750 × 382 | **l62 r62** | landscapeLeft | leading 62 |
| iPhone 17 Pro, landscapeRight | 750 × 382 | **l62 r62** | landscapeRight | trailing 62 |
| iPad Pro 11, окно | 417 × 1158 | t32 b20 **l0 r0** | portrait | none |
| iPad Pro 11, окно, запрошен landscape | 1210 × 397 | t10 b10 **l0 r0** | landscapeLeft | leading **0** |
| iPad Pro 11, `UIRequiresFullScreen` | без изменений | | | |

Первые две строки воспроизвели числа, уже записанные в исходнике — это сертифицирует пробник. Дальше: анализ §2.1 верен, изменяемое окно даёт нулевой bleed с любой стороны. Плюс две находки, которых в issue не было: `UIWindowScene.interfaceOrientation` **депрекейтнут** в SDK 27 (свапнул на `effectiveGeometry.interfaceOrientation`, доступен с iOS 16, гейт не нужен), и `UIRequiresFullScreen` на iPadOS 27 **игнорируется** — заметка в `AGENTS.md` про iPadOS 26 исправлена.

## 2. `.soft` против `.automatic`

`.automatic`, `.hard` и «без модификатора» дают **побайтово одинаковый** кадр; отличается только `.soft` — 5.7 % кадра, полоса ровно 0…150 pt под баром. Остальные три рисуют там волосяную линию, которая над логом читается как ещё один разделитель строк. **`.soft` остаётся**, причина записана рядом с модификатором. Сборка с ним стоит на телефоне — посмотри лог-консоль (Settings → Advanced).

## Чего не сделал

- **Третий размер снапшотов** — по твоему решению откатил, эталонов ровно 1632, `.prefire.yml` не тронут. Измеренная цена (+816 PNG / ~100 МБ LFS) записана в `CLAUDE.md` и `ios-27.md`.

`dockBleed` chooses **which** screen edge the docked tab reaches for, and it read `UIWindowScene.interfaceOrientation`. | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| iPhone 17 Pro, full screen, portrait | 402 × 778 | t62 b34 **l0 r0** | portrait | none |
| iPhone 17 Pro, landscapeLeft | 750 × 382 | **l62 r62** | landscapeLeft | leading 62 |
| iPhone 17 Pro, landscapeRight | 750 × 382 | **l62 r62** | landscapeRight | trailing 62 |
| iPad Pro 11, window | 417 × 1158 | t32 b20 **l0 r0** | portrait | none |
| iPad Pro 11, window, landscape requested | 1210 × 397 | t10 b10 **l0 r0** | landscapeLeft | leading **0** |
| iPad Pro 11, `UIRequiresFullScreen` set | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged |

The first two rows reproduce figures already recorded in the source, which is what certifies the probe before believing its new ones. The two readings then agreed in every configuration.

**The resized window is harmless.** Requesting landscape on iPadOS 27 rotates the interface inside a window whose shape on the display does not change, and the horizontal insets there are zero. - **`UIRequiresFullScreen` is ignored on iPadOS 27.** The same build reported the same 417 pt window with and without the key, so the iPad half of the probe recipe in `AGENTS.md` was wrong and is corrected.
